puzzles.prompt: What is the sum of all integers from 1 to 100 that are divisible by 3 or by 5?
puzzles.explanation: Multiples of 3: 33 terms summing to 3×(33×34/2) = 1,683. Multiples of 5: 20 terms, 5×(20×21/2) = 1,050. Multiples of 15 were counted twice: 6 terms, 15×21 = 315. Total = 1,683 + 1,050 − 315 = 2,418.

puzzles.prompt: If log₂(x) + log₂(x − 2) = 3, what is x?
puzzles.explanation: log₂(x(x − 2)) = 3, so x² − 2x = 8, giving (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0. x = −2 is impossible inside a logarithm, so x = 4.

puzzles.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², how high does it rise (in metres)?
puzzles.explanation: At the top the speed is zero: v² = u² − 2gh, so h = u²/(2g) = 400/20 = 20 m.

puzzles.prompt: In how many distinct ways can the letters of the word LEVEL be arranged?
puzzles.explanation: 5 letters with L repeated twice and E repeated twice: 5!/(2!×2!) = 120/4 = 30.

puzzles.prompt: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. What current does the battery supply?
puzzles.explanation: Parallel resistance = (6×3)/(6+3) = 2 Ω. Current = V/R = 12/2 = 6 A.

puzzles.prompt: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability of getting at least one six?
puzzles.explanation: P(no six) = (5/6)² = 25/36, so P(at least one six) = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36.

puzzles.prompt: If the day after tomorrow is a Sunday, what day was the day before yesterday?
puzzles.explanation: Day after tomorrow = Sunday, so today is Friday. Two days before Friday is Wednesday.

puzzles.prompt: f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x. At which value of x greater than 1 does f have a local minimum?
puzzles.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x − 1)(x − 3). f' changes from negative to positive at x = 3, so that's the local minimum (x = 1 is a maximum).

puzzles.prompt: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, …?
puzzles.explanation: First term 7, common difference 4. The nth term is 7 + (n − 1)×4, so the 10th is 7 + 36 = 43.

puzzles.prompt: Which cell organelle is the main site of aerobic respiration?
puzzles.explanation: Mitochondria carry out the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, producing most of the cell’s ATP — hence “powerhouse of the cell”.

puzzles.prompt: Insulin is secreted by which cells?
options: Alpha cells of the pancreatic islets
Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
puzzles.explanation: Beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans make insulin; alpha cells make glucagon, which has the opposite effect.

puzzles.prompt: In a dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes (AaBb × AaBb), what is the phenotypic ratio?
puzzles.explanation: Each gene independently gives a 3 : 1 ratio; combining them gives (3:1)×(3:1) = 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, as Mendel found.

puzzles.prompt: How many chromosomes are in a normal human somatic (body) cell?
puzzles.explanation: Human body cells are diploid: 23 pairs, so 46 chromosomes. Gametes carry 23.

puzzles.prompt: What is the structural and functional unit of the kidney?
puzzles.explanation: Each kidney has around a million nephrons, which filter blood and form urine.

puzzles.prompt: How many moles of water are in 36 g of water? (H = 1, O = 16)
puzzles.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = 2×1 + 16 = 18 g/mol. 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol.

puzzles.prompt: What is the hybridisation of carbon in methane (CH₄)?
puzzles.explanation: Carbon forms four equivalent single bonds in a tetrahedral shape (109.5°), which is sp³ hybridisation.

puzzles.prompt: Red blood cells from a donor with blood group O negative can be given to:
options: Recipients of any ABO and Rh group
puzzles.explanation: O negative red cells carry no A, B or Rh(D) antigens, so they are the universal red-cell donor type — used in emergencies before cross-matching.

puzzles.prompt: A 2 kg body moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy in joules?
puzzles.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

puzzles.prompt: Vitamin D deficiency in children causes:
puzzles.explanation: Without vitamin D, calcium isn’t absorbed well and growing bones soften and bend — rickets. Scurvy is vitamin C, beriberi B1, night blindness vitamin A.

puzzles.prompt: Which of these is NOT a function of the liver?
puzzles.explanation: The liver makes bile, stores glycogen and detoxifies; insulin comes from the pancreas.

puzzles.prompt: What is the pH of a 0.001 M solution of HCl (assume complete dissociation)?
A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 30 cm. What is its focal length?
puzzles.explanation: For a spherical mirror f = R/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm.

puzzles.prompt: In photosynthesis, the oxygen released comes from:
puzzles.explanation: Experiments with labelled oxygen (¹⁸O) showed the O₂ comes from splitting water molecules (photolysis) in the light reactions.

puzzles.prompt: A patient's resting heart rate is 52 beats per minute (adult normal: 60–100). This is called:
puzzles.explanation: A resting rate below 60 is bradycardia (fit athletes often have it). Above 100 is tachycardia.

puzzles.prompt: A child weighs 20 kg. The dose is 15 mg per kg. How many mg is one dose?
puzzles.explanation: 20 kg × 15 mg/kg = 300 mg. Always double-check weight-based doses for children.

puzzles.prompt: A patient's relative shouts at you because the doctor is late. What's the best first response?
options: Explain that you are very busy too
Acknowledge their worry, apologise for the wait and give a realistic update
Walk away until they calm down
puzzles.explanation: Acknowledging feelings and giving honest information de-escalates most conflicts. Security is for real threats.

puzzles.prompt: Three patients arrive at once. Who should be seen first?
options: A teenager with a sprained ankle
A 55-year-old with crushing chest pain and sweating
A playful child with two days of mild fever
An adult asking for a repeat prescription
puzzles.explanation: Triage puts possible life threats first. Chest pain with sweating could be a heart attack, where minutes matter.

puzzles.prompt: A drip of 1,000 ml must run over 8 hours. How many ml per hour?
puzzles.explanation: 1,000 ÷ 8 = 125 ml per hour.

puzzles.prompt: Is the shopkeeper liable?
options: Yes: there was a duty, a breach and harm caused by it
No: customers should watch where they walk
Only if the shopkeeper meant to hurt someone
puzzles.explanation: All three elements are present: a duty to customers, a breach (no warning sign) and harm caused by it. Intention is not needed for negligence.
puzzles.passage:
Principle: A person is liable for negligence if they owe someone a duty of care, breach that duty, and the breach causes harm.
Facts: A shopkeeper mops the floor during opening hours and puts up no warning sign. A customer slips and breaks a wrist.

puzzles.prompt: Is there a contract?
options: No, the offer had lapsed before B accepted
Yes, but only for half the price
No, because bikes cannot be sold by message
puzzles.explanation: The offer stated its own deadline. Once Friday passed it lapsed, and there was nothing left for B to accept on Saturday.
puzzles.passage:
Principle: An offer can be accepted only while it is open. An offer lapses after any time limit stated in it.
Facts: A messages B: "I will sell you my bike for ₹30,000. Offer valid till Friday." B replies "Accepted" on Saturday morning.

puzzles.prompt: What is the status of X's agreement?
options: Voidable at the option of X
Void for both parties from the start
Valid only if Y pays more
puzzles.explanation: Consent obtained through threats is not free. By the principle, X can choose to set the contract aside (or keep it).
puzzles.passage:
Principle: Consent obtained by coercion is not free consent. Such an agreement is voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so obtained.
Facts: Y threatens to harm X’s family unless X signs a sale deed for X’s land. X signs.

puzzles.prompt: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
puzzles.explanation: Part III (Articles 12–35) contains the Fundamental Rights. Part IV holds the Directive Principles of State Policy.

puzzles.prompt: Article 21 of the Constitution of India protects:
puzzles.explanation: Article 21: no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Courts have read many rights into it.

puzzles.prompt: Can the lender enforce the promissory note against the borrower?
options: Yes, a signed note is always binding
No, the agreement is void from the start
Only if the borrower turns 18 first
puzzles.explanation: Under the stated principle, an agreement with a minor is void ab initio — it never had legal force, so it cannot be enforced.
puzzles.passage:
Principle: An agreement with a minor (under 18) is void from the beginning (void ab initio).
Facts: A 16-year-old borrows ₹50,000 and signs a promissory note. The lender sues to recover the money.

puzzles.prompt: Has A committed theft?
options: Yes, A took property without consent
No, A had no dishonest intention
Yes, because umbrellas are movable property
puzzles.explanation: Theft needs dishonest intention. A honestly believed the umbrella was his own, so the mental element is missing.
puzzles.passage:
Principle: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of another's possession without consent, moves it, commits theft.
Facts: After a meeting, A picks up B's black umbrella from the stand, honestly believing it is his own identical umbrella.

puzzles.prompt: All lawyers are graduates. Some graduates are athletes. Which of these must be true?
options: Some graduates are lawyers, if any lawyer exists
puzzles.explanation: Only what follows from the premises must be true. Lawyers are a subset of graduates, so any lawyer is a graduate. Nothing links lawyers to athletes either way.

puzzles.prompt: Your client privately admits that a statement in their affidavit is false. What do you do?
options: Advise them it must be corrected, and refuse to help mislead the court
Drop the case without a word
puzzles.explanation: A lawyer owes a duty to the court as well as the client. You can keep the confidence but must not help present false evidence.

puzzles.prompt: A shop's revenue rose from ₹80 lakh to ₹1 crore. What was the percentage increase?
puzzles.explanation: Increase = ₹20 lakh. 20 ÷ 80 = 0.25 = 25%. (₹1 crore = ₹100 lakh.)

puzzles.prompt: ₹10,000 is invested at 10% a year, compounded annually. What is the amount after 2 years (₹)?
P is taller than Q. R is shorter than Q. S is taller than P. Who is the shortest?
puzzles.explanation: Order from tallest: S > P > Q > R. R is shortest.

puzzles.prompt: The average of 5 numbers is 40. One is removed and the average of the rest becomes 38. What number was removed?
puzzles.explanation: Total before = 5 × 40 = 200. Total after = 4 × 38 = 152. Removed = 200 − 152 = 48.

puzzles.prompt: Product A sells 1,000 units at ₹50 margin each. Product B sells 400 units at ₹150 margin each. Which earns more profit?
puzzles.explanation: A: 1,000 × 50 = ₹50,000. B: 400 × 150 = ₹60,000. B earns ₹10,000 more despite selling fewer units.

puzzles.prompt: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how many days do they take?
Roughly how did the service’s revenue change?
puzzles.explanation: Revenue = price × subscribers = 1.20 × 0.95 = 1.14 of the original: about 14% higher.
puzzles.passage: A streaming service raised its monthly price by 20%. Over the next quarter, its number of subscribers fell by 5%. Nothing else changed.

puzzles.prompt: Fixed costs are ₹2,00,000. Each unit sells for ₹500 and costs ₹300 to make. How many units must be sold to break even?
puzzles.explanation: Each unit contributes ₹500 − ₹300 = ₹200. 2,00,000 ÷ 200 = 1,000 units.

puzzles.prompt: Your team will miss a client deadline because a key colleague fell ill. What do you do?
options: Blame the colleague in the client call
Tell the client early, with a revised date and a plan
puzzles.explanation: Bad news gets worse with age. Early, honest communication with a credible plan protects trust.

puzzles.prompt: A city has 10 lakh households. 20% own a car. Half of car owners use a paid car wash, 4 times a month. How many paid washes happen each month?
puzzles.explanation: 10,00,000 × 20% = 2,00,000 cars. Half = 1,00,000 use paid washes. × 4 = 4,00,000 washes a month.

puzzles.prompt: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by which amendment?
puzzles.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble.

puzzles.prompt: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
puzzles.explanation: Under Article 108, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting.

puzzles.prompt: In which year did the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) begin?
puzzles.explanation: Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram for Dandi on 12 March 1930 to break the salt law.

puzzles.prompt: Through how many Indian states does the Tropic of Cancer pass?
puzzles.explanation: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram: 8 states.

puzzles.prompt: India's repo rate is set by the Monetary Policy Committee of:
puzzles.explanation: The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee sets the policy repo rate.

puzzles.prompt: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) is about:
puzzles.explanation: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj (rural local government). The 74th did the same for urban bodies.

puzzles.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
puzzles.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth’s surface — more than all the land combined.

puzzles.prompt: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
puzzles.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω): R = V/I.

puzzles.prompt: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
puzzles.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultan, founding the Mughal empire. He fought Rana Sanga at Khanwa in 1527.

puzzles.prompt: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
puzzles.explanation: Under Article 324, the President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners.

puzzles.prompt: A 200 m long train passes a pole in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
puzzles.explanation: Speed = 200/10 = 20 m/s. To convert to km/h multiply by 18/5: 20 × 3.6 = 72 km/h.

puzzles.prompt: What is the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 8% a year for 3 years (₹)?
What is the compound interest (the interest only, not the total) on ₹20,000 at 10% a year for 2 years, compounded annually (₹)?
A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹400 and sells it for ₹500. What is the profit percentage?
puzzles.explanation: Profit = ₹100 on a cost of ₹400. 100/400 = 25%.

puzzles.prompt: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 2. There are 45 boys. How many students are there in total?
puzzles.explanation: 3 parts = 45, so 1 part = 15. Total = 5 parts = 75.

puzzles.prompt: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours; pipe B empties it in 9 hours. With both open, how many hours to fill the empty tank?
puzzles.explanation: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18 of the tank per hour, so 18 hours.

puzzles.prompt: What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, what is tan θ? (Give a decimal.)
Solve for x: 3x − 7 = 2x + 5
puzzles.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: x − 7 = 5, so x = 12.

puzzles.prompt: Where i² = −1, what is (1 + i)²?
What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
puzzles.explanation: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next is +12 → 42. (Each term is n × (n + 1).)

puzzles.prompt: If CAT is written as DBU in a code, how is DOG written?
puzzles.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: C→D, A→B, T→U. So D→E, O→P, G→H: EPH.

puzzles.prompt: Pointing to a man, Meera says: "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is the man related to Meera?
puzzles.explanation: Her grandfather's only son is Meera's father. His son is Meera's brother.

puzzles.prompt: Ravi walks 4 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 4 km. How far is he from his starting point (km)?
puzzles.explanation: North 4, east 3, then south 4. The north and south legs cancel, leaving him 3 km east of the start.

puzzles.prompt: Which is the odd one out? 121, 144, 169, 196, 210
puzzles.explanation: 121, 144, 169 and 196 are perfect squares (11², 12², 13², 14²). 210 is not.

puzzles.prompt: Statements: Some pens are books. All books are bags. Conclusions: I. Some pens are bags. II. All bags are pens. Which follow?
puzzles.explanation: The pens that are books must also be bags, so I follows. Nothing says every bag is a pen, so II does not.

puzzles.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'BENEVOLENT'.
puzzles.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly.

puzzles.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Neither of the boys has done his homework.
Each of the students have a book.
She is more smarter than me.
puzzles.explanation: "Neither" and "each" take singular verbs ("has", not "have"). "Don't" should be "doesn't"; "more smarter" is a double comparative.

puzzles.prompt: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'SCARCE'.
puzzles.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; its opposite is abundant. The others are synonyms.

puzzles.prompt: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of deposits a bank must keep:
options: As cash balances with the RBI
As gold in its own vaults
puzzles.explanation: CRR is held with the RBI and earns no interest. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is kept by the bank in liquid assets such as government securities.

puzzles.prompt: In banking, KYC stands for:
puzzles.explanation: Know Your Customer: verifying identity and address to prevent fraud and money laundering.

puzzles.prompt: A customer earns ₹20,000 a month and already pays a ₹6,000 EMI. The bank caps total EMIs at 50% of income. What is the largest additional EMI they can take (₹)?
According to Piaget, children aged about 7–11 are in which stage of development?
puzzles.explanation: In the concrete operational stage children reason logically about concrete objects; abstract reasoning comes in the formal operational stage (11+).

puzzles.prompt: The 'Zone of Proximal Development' is associated with:
puzzles.explanation: Vygotsky described the gap between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with guidance — where teaching works best.

puzzles.prompt: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 covers children aged:
puzzles.explanation: The RTE Act (and Article 21A) guarantees free and compulsory education from 6 to 14.

puzzles.prompt: A pupil keeps failing in maths but draws beautifully. What is the best approach?
options: Label the child weak at maths
Use diagrams and visual methods to teach maths
puzzles.explanation: Good teaching builds on a learner’s strengths; visual methods can make abstract ideas concrete.

puzzles.prompt: On crowd duty at a festival you find a crying, lost child. What do you do first?
options: Keep the child safe with you and alert the control room for an announcement
Hand the child to a helpful stranger
Tell the child to wait by the gate
puzzles.explanation: The child’s safety comes first; stay with them and use official channels to find the family.

puzzles.prompt: A driver offers you ₹500 to ignore a traffic violation. What do you do?
options: Refuse and issue the challan as the law says
Let them go to earn goodwill
puzzles.explanation: Accepting is bribery, a crime. Enforce the law fairly and record the offence.

puzzles.prompt: Your patrol has one hour of water left. Base is three hours away; a stream is a 30-minute detour. Best decision?
options: Detour to refill and radio base with the new plan
puzzles.explanation: A short, safe detour fixes the real risk (dehydration). Telling base keeps everyone informed.

puzzles.prompt: What is the approximate speed of sound in air at room temperature?
puzzles.explanation: About 340 m/s. 3 × 10⁸ m/s is the speed of light.

puzzles.prompt: As District Collector during floods, village A (2,000 people) is cut off; village B (500 people) still has road access. You have one helicopter. What is the best plan?
options: Use the helicopter for A and send road convoys to B
puzzles.explanation: Match scarce resources to need: only air can reach A, while B can be supplied by road.

puzzles.prompt: Which best describes 'probity' in public life?
puzzles.explanation: Probity means strong moral principles and honesty — the core of trustworthy public service.

programs.name: MBBS (Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery)
programs.description: Five and a half years of anatomy, wards and night duties, including the internship. Entry through the fictional NEXT-Med exam.

programs.name: B.Sc Nursing
programs.description: Four years of clinical training on hospital wards. Open admission on school results; nurses are hired everywhere.

programs.name: B.Pharm (Bachelor of Pharmacy)
programs.description: Four years of chemistry, drug design and dispensing. Open admission; leads into pharmacies and pharma companies.

programs.name: BA LLB (five-year integrated law)
programs.description: Five years of constitutional law, contracts, moot courts and internships. Entry through the fictional CLAE exam.

programs.name: MBA (Master of Business Administration)
programs.description: Two intense years of case studies, finance, marketing and a summer internship. For graduates; entry through the fictional GMET.

programs.name: Commercial Pilot Licence training
programs.description: Eighteen months of ground school and 200 flying hours. Expensive, but it leads to the cockpit. Needs Health 55+.

loanProducts.name: Vidya Plus Professional Education Loan
loanProducts.description: For expensive professional courses (medicine, management, aviation). Repayment starts six months after the course ends; interest accrues throughout.

careers.name: Union Administrative Service officer
careers.description: Run a district, then a department, then perhaps the country. Enormous responsibility, transfers and a clipboard full of crises. Entry only through the USE.

careers.name: Union Police Service officer
careers.description: Lead a district police force: law and order, investigations and VIP duty at 3 a.m. Entry only through the USE.

careers.name: Union Revenue Service officer
careers.description: Income-tax investigations, raids and appeals. Numbers, law and nerve. Entry only through the USE.

careers.name: State administrative officer
careers.description: A Deputy Collector in your own state: land records, elections, disaster relief. Entry through the SSE.

careers.name: State police officer
careers.description: A Deputy Superintendent of Police leading a sub-division. Entry through the SSE.

careers.name: Income Tax Inspector
careers.description: Assessments, surveys and the occasional raid. Entry through the SST-GL.

careers.name: Central secretariat officer
careers.description: Files, notes and policy drafts in a central ministry. Steady hours and a pension. Entry through the SST-GL.

careers.name: Bank clerk
careers.description: Cash counters, passbooks and pension queues — the public face of a public-sector bank. Entry through the NBPE.

careers.name: Railway employee
careers.description: Tickets, timetables and platforms, then running a station. Open to anyone who clears the RRT.

careers.name: Police constable
careers.description: Beat patrols, festival duty and night checkpoints. Hard, honest work if you keep it honest. Entry through the SPCT.

careers.name: Armed forces officer
careers.description: Commissioned service in the armed forces: training, postings at the border and a lifetime of discipline. Entry through the NDE or CDE.

careers.name: Government school teacher
careers.description: Forty children, one blackboard and the chance to change lives. Secure, respected, underpaid only in the early years. Entry through the TET.

locations.name: Toppers' Coaching Hub
locations.description: Six floors of batches for every entrance and government exam, a photocopy shop and a lot of nervous parents.

actions.label: Engineering entrance batch
actions.description: Three hours of mechanics and calculus with a teacher who never runs out of chalk.

actions.label: Medical entrance batch
actions.description: Biology diagrams, organic reactions and a daily test.

actions.label: Law entrance batch
actions.description: Legal reasoning drills and newspaper editorials.

actions.label: MBA entrance batch
actions.description: Data interpretation sets and case discussions.

actions.label: Civil services foundation batch
actions.description: Polity, history, economy and answer-writing practice.

actions.label: Banking, SSC & railways batch
actions.description: Speed maths, reasoning shortcuts and general awareness.

actions.label: Teacher eligibility batch
actions.description: Child psychology, pedagogy and micro-teaching.

actions.label: Police & defence physical training
actions.description: Dawn runs, rope climbs and a drill instructor who remembers your name.

actions.label: Mock interview panel
actions.description: Three retired officers grill you about your hobbies and your hometown.

events.title: Results: UTAT Advanced
events.summary: The UTAT Advanced results are published.

premier.speaker: narrator
premier.text: Your rank is good enough. The Premier Institute of Technology — the one on the posters — has a seat with your name on it.

choices.label: Take the premier seat — pay the fees yourself (₹2,20,000/year).
Decline. Not this path, or not this year.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The UTAT Advanced results are out.

fail.speaker: narrator
fail.text: Not this time. The cut-off was higher than your score. It stings — and it's also just one attempt. Most people who clear exams like this failed one first.

conclusions.title: In Public Service
conclusions.text: You cleared an exam that thousands of people sat with you, and now you work for the public. The pay is steady, the files are endless and the transfers will come — but somewhere a person you will never meet gets a little more fairness because you showed up.
